Source [S1] explicitly defines the second-order polynomial as $Ax^2 + By^2 + Cz^2 + Dxy + Exz + Fyz + Gx + Hy + Iz + J$ and states that finding the integral amounts to finding the integrals of the coordinate moments: $x^2, y^2, z^2, xy, xz, yz, x, y, z,$ and $V$ (the volume, corresponding to the constant term $J$). All facts in the claim are present in the evidence.
